patch.sql:
select distinct
    c_custkey as customer_key,
    c_name as customer_name,
    c_address as address,
    c_phone as phone,
    c_nationkey as nation_key,
    c_mktsegment as market_segment,
    c_acctbal as account_balance
from {{ source('raw', 'customer') }}
patch.explanation: The raw.customer source contains 75 exact duplicate rows (same c_custkey and all other column values). The staging model stg_customers simply selected the source columns, propagating those duplicates, which caused the unique_stg_customers_customer_key check to fail. Since the duplicates are identical, they represent a delivery duplication and can be safely removed by deduplicating in the staging model. Using SELECT DISTINCT preserves the original column names and types while eliminating the duplicate rows, fixing the uniqueness check without altering any other logic.

Policy: identical duplicates are a delivery duplication; fix by deduplicating in the staging model.
